title: Aim a geared pointer whose gears have play
instruction: The + and - buttons turn the pointer through a small gearbox: each press turns the motor by the same unknown number of degrees, but the gears have play (backlash), so after a change of direction the motor turns some degrees before the pointer moves. The pointer was last turned with +. Turn the pointer to the angle on the red plate, and put the card showing the backlash in degrees on the red mat. Use at most 10 presses in total.
context: Positioning through gears with play (backlash) is everyday work on telescope mounts, machine-tool axes and valve actuators: after a change of direction the output lags the motor. The robot has to measure both the step and the play before committing its presses, then report the play.
setup: A white dial plate (13.6 x 23.6 cm) lies flat 40 cm in front of the arm bases, centred between them, printed with a protractor arc of radius 10 cm (0 deg toward the right arm, 90 deg straight ahead, 180 deg toward the left arm; a tick every 10 deg, long ticks every 30 deg) and a black pointer on a centre pivot; a red tick marks the target angle. Two push buttons (dark grey caps 3.6 x 3.6 cm, 3 cm tall) stand 22 cm in front of the bases, 5.5 cm left (marked -) and 5.5 cm right (marked +) of centre. A 3-digit red LED display 30 cm in front, centred, shows the pointer angle in whole degrees; a pink plate 12.5 cm to its right is printed with the target angle. Five white cards (5 x 5 x 2.4 cm) printed 0°, 2°, 4°, 6° and 8° lie in front of the left arm, and a 12 x 12 cm red mat lies 30 cm in front of the left arm's base. For seed 0 the pointer starts at 96 deg and the target is 70 deg.
scoring: 0: no button pressed and nothing touched. 0.25: a button is pressed or a card touched. 0.5: at least one reading: the pointer held still for 1 s after a press. 0.75: the angles read after each press, before the last press, leave only one gear model (step per press 5-12 deg, backlash 0-10 deg) consistent with the presses made, and the card showing the backlash is alone on the red mat. 1.0: the 0.75 condition holds, the display shows the target angle (within 1 deg) at the end, and at most 10 presses were used. The score is the highest level reached.
reset_notes: Hidden per trial (redrawn every trial from its seed): Step s (6-10 deg), backlash b (2, 4 or 6 deg), start angle 70-110 deg, gear engaged in the + direction. Target = start + b - j s (j = 3-5): reachable only while turning -. Pressing + once and computing the - presses from that step lands one step short whenever b/s > 0.5; and it takes the backlash to be 0. Budget 10 presses (oracle: 2 + j).
fidelity: The pointer is moved in code from a gear model (motor step, backlash) when a button press registers; a real build would use a stepper motor and a geared dial with an encoder display.
